records.issue_text: [BUG] The team-permission check uses && instead of ||, requiring the user to be both an admin AND an owner. A team admin who is not the team owner (and not the organizer or an attendee) calling addGuests on a team booking gets a 403 FORBIDDEN, even though admins are clearly intended to manage team bookings; the permission tier is silently narrowed to owners-only.
records.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the permission flag is computed as:
```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```
Using `&&` requires the user to be BOTH a team admin AND a team owner to pass this check. The subsequent gate:
```ts
if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;
```
means a team admin who is not also the team owner (and not organizer/attendee) will get 403, matching the finding.

records.issue_text: [BUG] Blacklisted guests are silently dropped rather than rejected, and the handler passes the unfiltered `guests` to sendAddGuestsEmails while persisting only uniqueGuests. A user who adds [good@example.com, blacklisted@example.com] sees 'Guests added' with no indication the blacklisted guest was excluded — no acceptance criterion or error message communicates the partial failure, so the user believes the guest was invited.
records.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, blacklisted emails are filtered out silently: `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(... && !blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest))`, and the handler only errors when `uniqueGuests.length === 0`, so mixed input like `[good, blacklisted]` will succeed without reporting that one was dropped. It also persists only `uniqueGuests` (`createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }`) but calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the unfiltered `guests`, making the persisted set and the “newGuests” parameter inconsistent.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The handler reads seatsPerTimeSlot/seatsShowAttendees from the event type but never enforces seat capacity when adding guests. On a seat-based event type, an organizer or attendee can add unlimited guests via this endpoint, exceeding seatsPerTimeSlot and producing attendee counts the seats logic elsewhere assumes are bounded — seat-count invariants silently break.
records.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` unconditionally appends attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }}}})` with no check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` / seat availability. Yet it includes `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` on the constructed `CalendarEvent` (`evt.seatsPerTimeSlot = booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`), indicating seat-based semantics exist but are not enforced here. This means seat-limited bookings can have their attendee count increased beyond capacity through this new endpoint.

records.issue_text: [BUG] prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId || 0 throws an unhandled Prisma NOT_FOUND error when booking.userId is null (e.g. system bookings). A booking with a null userId in the DB makes the addGuests mutation throw a raw Prisma error, returning a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of the 4xx the TRPCError-based contract elsewhere in this handler promises.
records.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the organizer is fetched via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is `null`/`undefined`, this becomes `id: 0`, which will cause `findFirstOrThrow` to throw a Prisma not-found error. That error is not wrapped in a `TRPCError` (unlike the earlier explicit `NOT_FOUND` for the booking), so it will bubble up as an internal error rather than a consistent 4xx TRPCError.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] List items use array index as the React key while entries are removed via splice, in a component whose only purpose is mutable row editing. Removing a middle email field while typing causes input state and focus to jump to the wrong row on the next render, biting any user managing 3+ emails; a stable id per row is the right data structure for a mutable list.
records.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the list renders `value.map((field, index) => ( <li key={index}> ... ))`, and removal mutates by index via `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`. A user who is a team admin but not the owner (or vice versa) gets FORBIDDEN on addGuests for team bookings where they are neither organizer nor attendee — the accepted intent (admins or owners can manage guests) is silently inverted, and since almost no one satisfies both roles the check is effectively dead code granting nothing.

In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the permission flag is computed as:
```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```
Using `&&` requires the user to be BOTH a team admin AND a team owner to pass this check. The subsequent gate:
```ts

```
means a team admin who is not also the team owner (and not organizer/attendee) will get 403, matching the finding.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `guests` array has no `.max()` cap, so the handler accepts an unbounded email list and fans it out into unbounded DB inserts, per-attendee translation fetches, N×M email sends, and calendar attendee updates on a request path. A single authenticated caller can submit thousands of emails, causing thousands of BookingAttendee rows and thousands of outbound emails plus a calendar API call with that attendee list (which the provider will reject at some size), turning one request into a mass-mailing/outbound amplification primitive; retries after the calendar reject re-trigger the fan-out since only exact-duplicate emails are filtered.
records.rationale: In the newly added endpoint, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts), and the handler then fans this input out into `attendees.createMany` DB inserts, per-attendee `getTranslation(...)` calls, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` with the full attendee list, and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which loops over attendees to send emails (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts and packages/emails/email-manager.ts).
